The table verbatim, six rows, Initial/Final: 'Less than 133%' 2.10/2.10 · 'At least 133% but less than 150%' 3.14/4.19 · 'At least 150% but less than 200%' 4.19/6.60 · 'At least 200% but less than 250%' 6.60/8.44 · 'At least 250% but less than 300%' 8.44/9.96 · 'At least 300% but not more than 400%' 9.96/9.96. §3.02 additionally gives the Required Contribution Percentage for plan years beginning in 2026 as 9.96%. ⚠️ CHAIN-CHECK CLAIM CORRECTED 2026-08-20 — the prior record said 'Each row's Final equals the next row's Initial'; that is TRUE AT 4 OF 5 SEAMS ONLY. Seam 1 (2.10 → 3.14) is a genuine statutory discontinuity, mirrored in §36B(b)(3)(A)(i)'s own base table (2.0 → 3.0 at the 133% boundary, read from the govinfo USCODE rendition) — expect 4-of-5, and never 'fix' a correct transcription to satisfy the false 5-of-5 checksum. DISCRIMINATING PROOF (per DND 012 — 9.96% alone is published identically in BOTH regimes and proves nothing): the table's SHAPE. It terminates at 'not more than 400%' and floors at 2.10%, which is the REVERTED regime; the enhanced 2021-2025 table has no 400% cap and floors at 0.00. ⚠️ But see discriminatingProof entry 4: the SHAPE identifies the regime the document was DRAFTED under, and a Rev. howToClear: Re-verify the CURRENT ACA enhanced-subsidy status against an enacted statute / IRS notice, then update verifiedOn + status + summary. Do NOT just bump the date — the law can flip the whole pre-65 model. Budget ~1 hour; the chain below is the one that works, each link independent. (1) Read §36B(b)(3)(A)(iii) and (c)(1)(E) at uscode.house.gov and note the granule's currentthrough marker — ⚠️ that marker is PER-TITLE and is NOT a verification ceiling (Title 26 read 119-83 while Title 42 read 119-102 on the same day); the operative rule is OLRC's own: no pending-update element means the section is current as shown, and the Classification Tables are the independent check. (2) Full-text sweep every public law above the real ceiling from govinfo, checking BODIES not status codes, with a positive control and a whitespace-flattened re-run (govinfo hard-wraps at ~72 columns, so a multi-word phrase can split and yield a false ZERO). (3) Confirm the law ceiling the same way, and cross-check archives.gov/federal-register/laws/current. (4) Check congress.gov presented-to-president.xml is empty — and read that leg as a BOUND on last-hours risk, not as proof. (5) Find the newest Rev. Proc. applicable-percentage table and confirm whether it terminates at 400%. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-02 — THE PRIOR VERSION OF THIS STEP SAID IT WAS 'AFFIRMATIVE EVIDENCE AND WORTH MORE THAN ANY NUMBER OF ABSENT-NEWS SEARCHES.' THAT IS FALSE and the counterexample is in discriminatingProof entry 4: Rev. Proc. 2022-34 published a reverted-shape table the day before the IRA restored the enhanced one. The Rev. Proc. LAGS the statute, so step 5 CORROBORATES; steps 1-3 are what prove. A re-verify that checks only step 5 has a documented one-day-miss failure mode. (6) RE-TYPE attests.applicablePercentage FROM the Rev. Proc. you opened in step 5, by hand, NEVER by copying src/engine/constants/health.ts. That table is re-issued ANNUALLY and clause (ii) indexing applies to it, so a new Rev. Proc. silently supersedes the shipped one; the bind arms in scripts/__tests__/verify-aca-status.test.ts compare your transcription against the constant and go RED on a one-sided edit. Copying from the constant makes that bind circular and defeats the gate. attests.enhancedPercentage is FIXED statute (clause (ii) does not apply) and only moves if Congress acts — but re-type it from the §36B granule you already have open in step 1, NOT from the constant: that attestation was circular until 2026-08-02 and said so in its own source line. (7) Check the Federal Register API (documents.json, publication_date ≥ the year start) for 'enhanced premium tax credit' and '36B' — a restoration forces agency rulemaking, so this is cheap negative space, and HHS's annual Notice of Benefit and Payment Parameters states the operative posture in plain language. (8) Every citation you write down must be retrieved and opened — see strickenCitations, both classes.
